provenance.abstraction_rationale: The selected affected API torch.compile is paired with the report's trigger and failure observation: compiling a model that performs advanced indexing and torch.sum produced an out-of-bounds read instead of an IndexError. The pattern normalizes that scenario around torch.compile and preserves the evidence-supported missing runtime index validation discussed in the report.
unresolved_information: No explicit root-cause claim was mapped in reported_diagnosis; the mechanism is derived from reporter/comment discussion.
No explicitly labelled reproduction section or captured reproduction artifact was mapped.

historical_conditions.statement: torch.compile is applied to a CPU model that indexes an input tensor of shape (2, 10) with an integer index tensor containing out-of-bounds index 3 for dimension 0 and then reduces the indexed result with torch.sum(dim=1).

defect_mechanism.description: Generated code from torch.compile performs indirect indexing x[idx] without a runtime bounds check when index values are unknown until execution, allowing out-of-bounds reads instead of raising IndexError.

observed_failure.description: The compiled model completed successfully and printed values containing NaN and large numbers that were labelled as an out-of-bound read, while the same non-compiled model raised IndexError for out-of-bounds index 3.

historical_observations.statement: The compiled model output was labelled as a successful out-of-bound read and contained NaN and large values at positions corresponding to the invalid index.
The same model executed without torch.compile raised IndexError: index 3 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 2.
